ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a large rectangle is divided by a vertical line segment and a horizontal line segment into four small rectangles, forming a 2×2 arrangement. The upper-left small rectangle is labeled with area 6, the upper-right small rectangle is labeled with area 14, the lower-right small rectangle is labeled with area 35, and the lower-left small rectangle is labeled with a question mark. Reasoning: Let the left column width be L, the right column width be R, the upper row height be T, and the lower row height be B. Then the upper-left area LT=6, the upper-right area RT=14, and the lower-right area RB=35. The required lower-left area is LB. Because the height in the same row is the same and the width in the same column is the same, there is the proportional relationship LT/RT = LB/RB, so 6/14 = LB/35. Therefore LB = 6×35/14 = 15.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the large rectangle is split by one vertical segment and one horizontal segment into a 2-by-2 grid. The visible area labels are 6 in the top-left rectangle, 14 in the top-right rectangle, 35 in the bottom-right rectangle, and a question mark in the bottom-left rectangle. Let the left and right column widths be L and R, and the top and bottom row heights be T and B. Then the shown areas give LT=6, RT=14, and RB=35. The unknown bottom-left area is LB. Since rectangles in the same row share height and rectangles in the same column share width, use the proportional area relation LT/R T = LB/RB, equivalently unknown = 6*35/14 = 15.
